causal_chain: A counterfactual ablation penalty forces the model to keep ranking margins stable when those selected supports are removed.
A support-selector can learn which historical edges actually justify each positive pair instead of treating all neighbors equally.
Sparse user histories make many positive items explainable by only a small subset of past interactions.
This should suppress brittle popularity/co-occurrence shortcuts and improve full-sort NDCG@10 on held-out items.
research_spec.competing_explanation: The gain comes from generic extra capacity, residual smoothing, or popularity debiasing rather than from learning a support-sensitive, counterfactually stable explanation of each positive interaction.
discriminative_predictions: A pure residual/dual-path control without counterfactual support-ablation training should underperform the proposed model even when parameter count is matched.
If the mechanism is real, removing the learned support mask at test time should hurt ranking much more than removing a same-sized residual branch.
Improvements should concentrate on sparse users, multi-interest users, and long-tail positives rather than being uniform across all users.
expected_evidence: A larger margin gap between the proposed model and the matched control when support-disagreement is high.
Better NDCG@10 on sparse-user and long-tail slices than on dense-user slices relative to control.
Lower loss sensitivity under leave-one-support-out ablations for held-out positives.
research_spec.falsifier: If the matched control with the same backbone and parameter budget matches or beats the proposal on full-sort NDCG@10, and the proposal shows no ablation-stability advantage on support-removed positives, the mechanism is not supported.
research_spec.high_change_justification: The accepted gap was that prior frontier/known-good packages were resource-deferred without mechanism-effect updates, and earlier fresh realizations lacked an explicit isolatable wedge and executable mechanism-off. Closing that gap requires a custom support-selection plus counterfactual stability objective, not just a configuration tweak of an existing profile.
research_spec.hypothesis: A pairwise recommender that learns per-positive support selection and trains margins to remain stable under support ablation will rank better than a standard LightGCN/BPR-style control because it captures which historical evidence truly supports each positive while rejecting brittle shortcut co-occurrence.

research_spec.mechanism_change: Add a learned support selector and a counterfactual support-ablation stability objective on top of a LightGCN-style pairwise CF backbone.
research_spec.mechanism_off_definition: A matched LightGCN/BPR model with dual-path or residual scoring only, but no learned support selection and no ablation-stability regularizer.

causal_chain: Edge dropout perturbs propagation paths and reduces overconfident co-occurrence shortcuts.
Rank-aware weighting concentrates learning signal on mistakes that matter most for top-10 ordering.
The effect should be strongest where sparse histories make shortcut reliance most harmful.
Their combination should improve full-sort NDCG@10 when the backbone is otherwise fixed.
research_spec.competing_explanation: Any gain comes mainly from generic regularization via edge dropout, not from rank-aware optimization.
discriminative_predictions: If rank-aware optimization is causal, the combined profile will retain a larger NDCG@10 advantage over an edge-dropout-only variant than over a rank-aware-only variant.
If the competing explanation is right, edge-dropout-only and combined variants should perform similarly after controlling for training stochasticity.
The lift should concentrate on sparse-history users and the top of the ranked list, not appear as a uniform shift across all users and cutoffs.
expected_evidence: Ablation on the frozen split showing combined > edge-dropout-only and combined > rank-aware-only on full-sort NDCG@10.
Top-k sensitivity consistent with rank-aware training affecting early ranking more than tail ordering.
User-sparsity stratification showing the largest gain in the sparsest bucket.
research_spec.falsifier: No improvement over LIGHTGCN or one-sided ablations on full-sort NDCG@10, or gains that do not track sparsity/top-k sensitivity.
research_spec.high_change_justification: No high-change change is required; this is an exact composition already expressible in the active profile catalog.
research_spec.hypothesis: A LightGCN recommender with edge-dropout propagation and rank-aware pairwise weighting will improve full-sort NDCG@10 on ML-1M by reducing brittle co-occurrence shortcuts while emphasizing the ranking mistakes that matter most at the top of the list.
implementation_requirements: Add stochastic edge dropout during propagation.
Extend the LightGCN training path in the accepted RecBole runtime.

research_spec.matched_control_requirement: Same frozen ML-1M split, same train-only fitting, same pairwise input regime, and same full-sort NDCG@10 evaluator, with the control using plain LightGCN without edge dropout or rank-aware weighting.
research_spec.mechanism_change: Combine stochastic edge-dropout propagation with rank-aware pairwise optimization in the LightGCN backbone.
research_spec.mechanism_off_definition: LightGCN with standard propagation and standard pairwise ranking, with neither edge dropout nor rank-aware weighting enabled.
research_spec.minimal_testable_wedge: Compare the combined profile against plain LightGCN and one-factor ablations on the frozen split, then inspect NDCG@10 by user-history sparsity.
research_spec.research_question: Can an exact LightGCN composition that adds edge dropout and rank-aware pairwise weighting beat plain LightGCN under the frozen ML-1M full-sort top-10 protocol?
research_spec.resource_hypothesis: The mechanism should fit within the 10 GPU-minute / 30 wall-minute budget on ML-1M using the accepted runtime and standard LightGCN-scale training.
